mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months indicates a weak labor market, reducing consumer demand and corporate profit margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 falling for two consecutive quarters) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 combined with a monthly unemployment rate below 4% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflation risk, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS > 200000 and UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index above 0.4% signals accelerating inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to consider tightening monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.4% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary easing.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines for three consecutive months and monetary policy is not easing.
